uscg.desc: General/Miscellaneous From: 2026-10-13 To: 2026-12-31 Location: 41-26-37.572N/071-20-37.536W 41-22-38.388N/071-18-48.780W 41-22-43.032N/071-27-26.640W 41-26-34.764N/071-24-57.096W 41-26-37.572N/071-20-37.536W Anduril Industries will conduct autonomous underwater vehicle testing in Rhode Island Sound from October 1, 2026, through December 31, 2026, daily from 0600 to 1800. Operations will involve a 19-foot autonomous underwater vehicle and support vessel F/V VOYAGER. The operating area is bounded by the approximate positions listed above. Mariners are requested to use caution when transiting the area. F/V VOYAGER may be contacted on VHF-FM channels 16 and 13. uscg.title: Providence River - Seekonk River/General/Bridges/Construction
uscg.desc: RHODE ISLAND- WASHINGTON BRIDGE (RIDOT BRIDGE NO. 700) – SEEKONK RIVER- General Construction – Rhode Island Department of Transportation (RIDOT) will begin preliminary construction work for the new Washington Bridge. From May 18, 2026, to June 29, 2029, there will be ongoing bridge construction operations Monday-Friday from 7:00 a.m.-4:30 p.m. Construction equipment and barges will be positioned outside of the navigation channel. For the next three months, there will be no reduction to the bridge horizontal or vertical clearances and no closures to the navigation channel. Mariners are advised to exercise caution and reduce wake when transiting the area. Mariners with questions or concerns can contact the contractor via marine radio VHF-FM Ch 16 or call Andy Kerr, General Superintendent at (860) 912-7299.

Mariners requiring full horizontal clearance can contact the contractor via marine radio VHF-FM Ch 13/16 or by calling (410) 294-6092 or (207) 356-0242. Mariners are advised to exercise caution and reduce wake when transiting the area.

uscg.title: New Bedford Channel - New Bedford Harbor Channel/General/Marine Construction (Excluding Bridges)/Dredging
uscg.desc: General/Marine Construction (Excluding Bridges)/Dredging From: 2026-10-21 To: 2027-07-09 DW White Construction Inc. will conduct intermittent disposal of material into CAD Cell 3 in the Acushnet River, at approximate position 41°37'27.37"N, 070°54'52.10"W, from October 23, 2026, through July 8, 2027. Operations will occur Monday through Friday, 6:00 a.m. to 11:00 p.m. Equipment on scene may include the push boats SHEELAGH M and ERIN ASHLEY; spud barges KS1502 and POSEIDON SECTIONAL; barges LITTLE JEFF and 61B; and a Caterpillar 390 excavator. Narragansett Bay-

.REST OF TONIGHT...W winds 5 to 10 kt. Waves 1 foot or less. 
.FRI...W winds 5 to 10 kt. Waves 1 foot or less. 
.FRI NIGHT...NW winds 5 to 10 kt, becoming N after midnight.
Waves 1 foot or less. 
.SAT...NE winds around 5 kt, becoming SE around 5 kt in the
afternoon. Waves 1 foot or less. 
.SAT NIGHT...SE winds around 5 kt. Waves 1 foot or less. 
.SUN...E winds 5 to 10 kt. Waves 1 foot or less, then around 2 ft
in the afternoon. A chance of rain in the afternoon. 
.SUN NIGHT...E winds 10 to 15 kt with gusts up to 20 kt,
increasing to 15 to 20 kt with gusts up to 30 kt after midnight.
Waves 2 to 4 ft. Rain.
.MON...N winds 15 to 20 kt with gusts up to 30 kt. Waves around
3 ft, except 4 to 6 ft at the bay entrance. Rain.
.MON NIGHT...NW winds 15 to 20 kt with gusts up to 30 kt. Waves
around 3 ft, except 4 to 6 ft at the bay entrance. A chance of
rain. 
.TUE AND TUE NIGHT...NW winds 15 to 20 kt with gusts up to 30 kt,
becoming N 10 to 15 kt with gusts up to 20 kt. Waves 2 to 3 ft.  

Seas are reported as significant wave height, which is the
average of the highest third of the waves. Individual wave
heights may be more than twice the significant wave height.
